clue.text: Cake cooked by the French with a German centre

parts.note: something cooked has been made, as in 'made a meal'

indicators.note: with a German centre means the German word goes into the middle of the French one

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for 'the'
ein is the German word for 'a'

explanation.surface: A recipe note about a cake baked by French cooks with a German filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like an anagram signal but simply means made; 'with a German centre' puts the German article in the middle of the French one, making LEINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A madeleine is a small shell-shaped French sponge cake, made famous by Proust.

clue.text: Way to acquire resources

definitions.meaning: a method or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: How to come by money.
explanation.definitionFit: Means is both a method used to an end and a person's financial resources.

clue.text: Hurt to see mother growing old

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
aged means old, advanced in years

explanation.surface: Someone pained to watch their mother age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see' only links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Damaged means harmed or injured, as hurt can be used of things as well as people.

clue.text: Tall pine

definitions.meaning: to yearn for, as in pine for home

explanation.surface: A lofty pine tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Long means tall in extent, and to long is to yearn or pine.

clue.text: Letter arranging to return in first-class accommodation

indicators.note: accommodation says the reversed mark houses the reordered word
return says the first-class mark is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI in crosswords

indicators.note: arranging says the next little word has its letters reordered

explanation.surface: A letter requesting a return to first-class lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation' is a noun used to signal that the reversed first-class mark holds the reordered little word; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Neckwear tied on a roll etc

indicators.note: tied says the words are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A tie and collar arranged on a bread roll and other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tied' rearranges ON A ROLL ETC; an ETON COLLAR is the stiff wide collar once worn at Eton, the English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eton collar is a broad starched collar worn outside a jacket, an item of neckwear.

clue.text: Girl turned over one in the grass

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one inside the turned girl
turned over says the word for a girl is read backwards

parts.note: a lass is a girl
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl rolling over in the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' makes SSAL from LASS, and 'in' puts I inside after the first S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is an agave plant whose fibre makes rope; loosely it is called a grass, as in sisal grass.

clue.text: Replace deputy

definitions.meaning: to put one thing in place of another

explanation.surface: Putting a stand-in in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Substitute is a verb meaning replace and a noun meaning a stand-in or deputy.

clue.text: Tales of riot 'e fomented aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard puts the jumbled letters inside the steamship

parts.note: SS is a steamship

indicators.note: fomented means stirred up, so the letters are stirred into new order

explanation.surface: Yarns of a mutiny he stirred up on board a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fomented' rearranges RIOT E into TORIE, and 'aboard' puts it in SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories are tales, narratives told for entertainment.

clue.text: Fell in love, but became discouraged

explanation.surface: A lover whose romance went sour.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's heart is to fall in love; to lose heart is to become disheartened.

clue.text: Means of defence against kicks by army footwear

parts.note: ammunition is what a defender fires, and figuratively anything used to defend a case
boots, as a verb, means kicks

explanation.surface: Something to protect you against being kicked by soldiers' boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' and 'by' only join the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammunition boots were the heavy hobnailed standard-issue boots worn by British soldiers.

clue.text: Master tells epic tale with a different ending

indicators.note: with a different ending says the last letter of the tale's word is swapped for another

parts.note: a saga is a long epic story

explanation.surface: A master storyteller recounts an epic, changing how it finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: SAGA has its final A changed to E; 'tells' only joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A sage is a wise teacher, a master whose learning others follow.

clue.text: Caledonian author and his characters

parts.note: Sir Walter Scott was the ... novelist who wrote Ivanhoe

indicators.note: characters is read as the letters of the next word, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A novelist from Scotland and the people in his books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' rearranges HIS into ISH. Caledonia is the old Latin name for Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonian is a poetic or formal adjective for things belonging to Scotland.

clue.text: Expert performance with no comeback?

parts.note: a tennis serve so good the opponent cannot return it

explanation.surface: A masterly show that leaves critics speechless.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace in tennis is a serve the receiver cannot touch, so there is no return.

clue.text: Is a teetotaller surrounded by beer barrels here?

definitions.text: Is a teetotaller surrounded by beer barrels here?

parts.words: Is a teetotaller surrounded by beer barrels here?
parts.note: a non-drinker literally riding on a brewer's dray loaded with casks

explanation.surface: An abstainer stranded among casks of ale.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means abstaining from alcohol, from the old water wagon; a brewer's dray puns on it.

clue.text: Powerful Italians once rejected Article 50, pertaining to healing

parts.note: the Medici were the ruling banking family of Renaissance Florence

indicators.note: rejected says the article is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Renaissance grandees throwing out a treaty article on health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article 50' looks like the Brexit treaty clause but splits into two pieces, and only the article is 'rejected'.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicinal is the adjective for things that have healing properties or relate to medicine.

clue.text: Not-to-be-forgotten amble about Rome, perhaps

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of amble and Rome are shuffled

explanation.surface: An unforgettable stroll around Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges AMBLE ROME; 'perhaps' only hints that the stroll is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Memorable describes something worth remembering, hard to forget.

clue.text: Operatic heroine cast down about love?

indicators.note: about says the jumbled word goes round the letter for love
down here means knocked over, so the letters of cast are disordered

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A downcast opera heroine, perhaps disappointed in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' rearranges CAST into TSCA, and 'about' wraps it round O after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is the singer heroine of Puccini's opera of the same name.

clue.text: Is unhappy about doctors including exercise

indicators.note: including says one piece sits inside the doctors

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, so MOS are doctors
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone gloomy about doctors who insist on exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To mope is to be listless and dejected, sulking around in low spirits.

clue.text: Moans from model about aircraft noise

indicators.note: about says the sounded word goes round the model
noise says the word for aircraft is taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: planes are aircraft
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: Complaints from a fashion model about the din of jets overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noise' gives PLAINS from PLANES, and 'about' wraps it round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaints are laments or complaints, a literary word for moans.

clue.text: Strongly experienced entre-left alignment

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Strongly experienced entre-left alignment (9)': the wordplay needs 'centre' (HEART) + anagram of LEFT, but the C is missing and neither a scan nor a search gives the printed text.

clue.text: Clean break, having second thoughts about embrace

indicators.note: break says the letters of clean are broken up
about says the second thoughts are turned round

parts.note: a PS, postscript, adds second thoughts to a letter

explanation.surface: A couple splitting cleanly, then reconsidering a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges CLEAN into ENCLA, and 'about' turns PS into SP; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Enclasp is an old verb meaning to hold in an embrace.

clue.text: Soldier found with missiles at back of auditorium

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, so a soldier in that corps
arrows are missiles shot from a bow

explanation.surface: An armed soldier spotted at the back of a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found with' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear rows are the seats furthest from the stage, at the back of a hall.

clue.text: Measure required to secure some extra credit

indicators.note: to secure some says the answer is held inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something needed to earn a little extra credit.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Measure required to secure' as the definition, but only 'Measure' defines; 'to secure some' signals the run held in 'extra credit', with 'required' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, a measure of about 4,047 square metres.

clue.text: Quarter bringing rate problem for consumer

parts.note: east is a compass quarter, written E

indicators.note: problem says the letters of rate are in disorder

explanation.surface: A district troubled by its tax rate for shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges RATE into ATER; 'bringing' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An eater is one who consumes food, a consumer.

clue.text: Play about cat's-paw, for instance

indicators.note: about says the word is turned the other way

parts.note: a cat's-paw is someone used as a tool by another

explanation.surface: A drama about a cat's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: LOOT is Joe Orton's black comedy of 1965.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is a well-known stage play by Joe Orton.

clue.text: Stage in favourite's rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise says the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a pet is a favourite; with the 's it gives pet's

explanation.surface: A stage in the climb of a favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a stage in a process or progression.

clue.text: Firm agreement a publisher might welcome

definitions.meaning: a contract that legally binds both sides
a deal for binding books, which a publisher needs

explanation.surface: A publisher pleased with a deal that sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: A binding contract is legally enforceable; a publisher also contracts out book binding.

clue.text: Girl otherwise taking one in

indicators.note: taking one in says the word for otherwise swallows the numeral

parts.note: else means otherwise, as in 'or else'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl who, by contrast, takes someone in.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside ELSE after the S; 'in' completes 'taking ... in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a girl's name, a pet form of Elizabeth.

clue.text: Bearer of correspondence about college journal

indicators.note: about says the college's name is turned round

parts.note: Eton College is the English public school
a paper is a newspaper or journal

explanation.surface: A school magazine carrying letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it turns ETON into NOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Notepaper is writing paper, which carries a letter's words.
